body: The Anil Dhirubhai Ambani group (ADAG) was valued near Rs 1 lakh cr+ at the Jan 2008 peak (Reliance Power's Rs 450 IPO was oversubscribed ~70x and fell below issue on listing). Over 2008-2020 group stocks (RCom, Reliance Capital, Reliance Infra, Reliance Home Finance) lost 95-99%. Reliance Capital peaked ~Rs 2,700+ (Jan 2008, unverified exact) and traded in single digits by 2020. RBI superseded its board on 29 Nov 2021; Hinduja's IIHL won with a ~Rs 9,650 cr plan (NCLT Feb 2024; completed Mar 2025), wiping equity. SEBI (Aug 2024) banned Anil Ambani and 24 entities for 5 years and fined him Rs 25 cr for diverting Reliance Home Finance money via 'general purpose corporate loans' to group-linked entities with weak financials. Visible flags: (1) GPCL loans from RHFL/RCap rising from ~Rs 900 cr to ~Rs 7,900 cr in a year to thinly capitalised borrowers; (2) auditor PwC resigned from RCap and RHFL in 2019 citing concerns it couldn't resolve; (3) near-100% promoter pledges; (4) RCom's 2G-era debt and failed asset sales (Jio spectrum deal blocked); (5) rating downgrades to D in 2019; (6) intra-group cross-holdings and guarantees. Lesson: lending subsidiaries of conglomerates lend to the conglomerate; auditor resignation with stated reasons is near-certain disqualifier.

data.early_signals: GPCL loans to group shells; PwC resignation 2019; ~100% pledges; rating cuts; RCom debt
data.lesson: Group NBFCs fund the group; auditor exit = sell

title: Reliance Capital / Anil Ambani group (2008-2025)
